layers.name: Interaction Layer
layers.plainEnglish: How users, agents, APIs, files, tools, and external systems communicate with the agent ecosystem.
layers.businessPurpose: This is the front door and communication fabric of an agentic system.

layers.name: Runtime Layer
layers.plainEnglish: Where agents reason, plan, remember, call tools, execute workflows, and perform work.
layers.businessPurpose: This is where AI-driven work and operational decisions happen.

layers.name: TrustOps Layer
layers.plainEnglish: The governance, monitoring, approval, identity, policy, and accountability layer for trusted autonomy.
layers.businessPurpose: This is the seatbelt, dashboard, brakes, and audit evidence for agentic systems.

components.name: Orchestrator
components.whatItIs: Breaks the top-level goal into subtasks and decides which agent or tool handles each one.
components.whyItMatters: Orchestrator helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Goal manipulation via prompt injection
topRisks.impact: An attacker rewrites the plan the orchestrator is working from, silently redirecting the entire system toward their own objective instead of the user's.
topRisks.mitigation: Separate trusted instructions from untrusted content; validate plans against an allow-listed goal schema before execution.

topRisks.name: Single point of failure
topRisks.impact: Because every agent depends on it, compromising or crashing the orchestrator takes down or misdirects the whole system at once.
topRisks.mitigation: Add plan-integrity checks, redundancy, and circuit breakers so a single bad plan can't cascade.

topRisks.name: Insecure delegation logic
topRisks.impact: Weak rules for choosing which agent gets a subtask let an attacker steer sensitive work toward a weaker or compromised agent.
topRisks.mitigation: Base delegation on verified capability and trust tiers, not on agent self-reported claims.

components.name: Sub-Agents
components.whatItIs: Specialized agents that carry out the subtasks the orchestrator assigns.
components.whyItMatters: Sub-Agents helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Excessive agency
topRisks.impact: An agent is granted broader permissions than its task requires, so a single manipulated instruction can trigger high-impact actions like sending money or deleting data.
topRisks.mitigation: Scope each agent's permissions tightly to the minimum needed for its specific role, and re-evaluate scope per task.

topRisks.name: Role confusion / impersonation
topRisks.impact: A malicious message convinces one agent it is actually another, trusted agent, causing it to accept instructions it should reject.
topRisks.mitigation: Give every agent a signed, verifiable identity that other agents check before trusting a message.

topRisks.name: Insecure inter-agent trust
topRisks.impact: Agents accept output from other agents at face value, so one manipulated agent can quietly poison the reasoning of every agent downstream.
topRisks.mitigation: Treat inter-agent messages as untrusted input and apply the same validation used for external data.

components.name: Tool-Calling Layer
components.whatItIs: The interface agents use to call external functions, APIs, and code.
components.whyItMatters: Tool-Calling Layer helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Tool poisoning
topRisks.impact: A malicious or compromised tool definition includes hidden instructions that hijack the calling agent the moment the tool is invoked.
topRisks.mitigation: Pin tool definitions, verify their source/signature, and diff them against a known-good baseline before use.

topRisks.name: Arbitrary code execution
topRisks.impact: A code-execution tool lets an attacker-controlled instruction run unrestricted code on the host system.
topRisks.mitigation: Run tool execution inside a hardened sandbox with no default access to secrets, network, or the filesystem.

topRisks.name: Unvalidated trust in tool output
topRisks.impact: Agents treat whatever a tool returns as ground truth, so a spoofed or manipulated tool response can steer later reasoning unchecked.
topRisks.mitigation: Validate and type-check tool outputs before they re-enter the agent's context.

components.name: Memory / Context Store
components.whatItIs: Persists conversation history, long-term memory, and embeddings across turns and sessions.
components.whyItMatters: Memory / Context Store helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Memory poisoning
topRisks.impact: An attacker writes malicious content into long-term memory once, and it keeps influencing agent behavior across every future session that reads it.
topRisks.mitigation: Validate and provenance-tag anything written to persistent memory; treat recalled memory as untrusted input.

topRisks.name: Cross-session data leakage
topRisks.impact: Context meant for one user or task bleeds into another session, exposing private data to the wrong party.
topRisks.mitigation: Strictly partition memory stores per user/tenant with enforced access boundaries.

topRisks.name: Persistent prompt injection
topRisks.impact: A prompt injection is stored rather than transient, so it keeps firing every time that memory is recalled, long after the original interaction.
topRisks.mitigation: Sanitize content before storage and periodically re-validate stored memory against current policy.

components.name: Inter-Agent Comms
components.whatItIs: The channel agents use to pass messages, requests, and results to one another.
components.whyItMatters: Inter-Agent Comms helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Man-in-the-middle injection
topRisks.impact: A party intercepts the message bus and injects or alters instructions in transit between two legitimate agents.
topRisks.mitigation: Encrypt and authenticate the transport layer end to end between agents.

topRisks.name: Message spoofing
topRisks.impact: An attacker crafts a message that appears to come from a trusted agent, getting other agents to act on forged instructions.
topRisks.mitigation: Sign inter-agent messages and verify sender identity before acting on message content.

topRisks.name: Lack of message integrity checks
topRisks.impact: Without checksums or signatures, corrupted or subtly altered messages pass through unnoticed and change downstream behavior.
topRisks.mitigation: Add integrity verification (hashes/signatures) on every inter-agent message.

components.name: Retrieval / RAG
components.whatItIs: Fetches external documents or data to ground agent responses in current information.
components.whyItMatters: Retrieval / RAG helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.
whatCouldGoWrong: Indirect prompt injection via retrieved content
Data poisoning of the knowledge base

topRisks.name: Indirect prompt injection via retrieved content
topRisks.impact: A document the system retrieves contains hidden instructions that the agent follows as if the user had typed them.
topRisks.mitigation: Isolate retrieved content as data, not instructions, and strip or flag embedded imperative language.

topRisks.name: Data poisoning of the knowledge base
topRisks.impact: An attacker seeds the retrieval corpus itself, so future queries reliably surface manipulated content.
topRisks.mitigation: Control write-access to the knowledge base and monitor it for anomalous or injected content.

topRisks.name: Source spoofing
topRisks.impact: Retrieved content is presented as authoritative when its actual source cannot be verified, misleading both the agent and the end user.
topRisks.mitigation: Track and surface provenance for every retrieved passage.

components.name: Execution Sandbox
components.whatItIs: Isolates code execution, browsing, and file operations from the host and from other agents.
components.whyItMatters: Execution Sandbox helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Sandbox escape
topRisks.impact: A flaw in the isolation layer lets agent-executed code break out and act directly on the host system.
topRisks.mitigation: Use hardened, regularly patched isolation technology and least-privilege container configuration.

topRisks.name: Privilege escalation
topRisks.impact: Code running in the sandbox finds a path to elevate its own permissions beyond what was granted.
topRisks.mitigation: Run sandboxed processes as non-root with no unnecessary capabilities, and audit for escalation paths.

topRisks.name: Insufficient isolation between agents
topRisks.impact: Multiple agents share a runtime environment, so one compromised agent can read or tamper with another's execution.
topRisks.mitigation: Give each agent (or task) its own isolated execution context rather than a shared runtime.

components.name: External Integrations
components.whatItIs: Connections to outside services — email, calendars, payments, ticketing, and more.
components.whyItMatters: External Integrations helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.
whatCouldGoWrong: Data exfiltration via a legitimate channel

topRisks.name: Data exfiltration via a legitimate channel
topRisks.impact: An attacker uses a legitimate, already-authorized integration (e.g. email or file-sharing) to quietly move sensitive data out — traffic that looks completely normal.
topRisks.mitigation: Monitor outbound data volume/destination patterns on integrations, not just their authorization status.

topRisks.name: Over-permissioned API scopes
topRisks.impact: Integrations are granted far more access than any given task needs, so a manipulated agent can take actions well outside its intended purpose.
topRisks.mitigation: Request the narrowest OAuth/API scopes possible and review them regularly.

topRisks.name: Third-party supply chain compromise
topRisks.impact: A vulnerability or breach at the integrated service propagates directly into your agent system through the trusted connection.
topRisks.mitigation: Vet integration partners, monitor advisories, and limit blast radius with scoped credentials.

components.name: Credentials & Secrets
components.whatItIs: API keys, tokens, and service credentials that let agents authenticate to tools and integrations.
components.whyItMatters: Credentials & Secrets helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.
whatCouldGoWrong: Secret leakage via logs or output

topRisks.name: Secret leakage via logs or output
topRisks.impact: A credential ends up in a debug log, error message, or model output, giving anyone who can read that output the keys themselves.
topRisks.mitigation: Scrub secrets from logs and outputs automatically; never place raw credentials in prompts or context.

topRisks.name: Long-lived static credentials
topRisks.impact: Credentials that never expire remain useful to an attacker indefinitely once stolen, with no natural window of exposure.
topRisks.mitigation: Use short-lived, automatically rotated tokens instead of static keys.

topRisks.name: Credential reuse across agents
topRisks.impact: The same key is shared by many agents, so compromising the weakest one gives an attacker access everywhere that key works.
topRisks.mitigation: Issue distinct, narrowly scoped credentials per agent so compromise doesn't generalize.

components.name: Human-in-the-Loop
components.whatItIs: Checkpoints where a person reviews or approves an agent's proposed action before it executes.
components.whyItMatters: Human-in-the-Loop helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Bypassable confirmation step
topRisks.impact: The approval step can be routed around programmatically, for instance by an agent calling a lower-level function that skips the check entirely.
topRisks.mitigation: Enforce approval at the permission layer itself, not just in the conversational flow that's easy to sidestep.

topRisks.name: Approval fatigue / rubber-stamping
topRisks.impact: When approval requests are frequent and repetitive, reviewers start clicking approve out of habit rather than genuine review.
topRisks.mitigation: Reserve human review for genuinely high-risk actions and make requests specific enough to actually evaluate.

topRisks.name: Unclear accountability
topRisks.impact: When something goes wrong, it's unclear whether the human approver, the agent, or the system designer is responsible for the outcome.
topRisks.mitigation: Log exactly what was shown to the approver at decision time, not just that approval occurred.

components.name: Agent Identity & AuthZ
components.whatItIs: Issues, verifies, scopes, and revokes agent identities and delegated authority for actions.
components.whyItMatters: Agent Identity & AuthZ helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Rogue agent registration
topRisks.impact: An attacker enrolls an untrusted agent into the environment and makes it appear legitimate to orchestrators, tools, or other agents.
topRisks.mitigation: Require signed registration, verified ownership, approval workflows, and continuous inventory reconciliation for agent identities.

topRisks.name: Broken delegated authorization
topRisks.impact: An agent receives authority from another agent without a task-bound policy check, allowing privilege to spread beyond the original intent.
topRisks.mitigation: Bind delegated permissions to task, actor, time, data scope, and action type; re-check authorization at every sensitive call.

topRisks.name: Stale or revoked token reuse
topRisks.impact: A token that should no longer be trusted still works, letting compromised agents continue acting after deactivation or scope changes.
topRisks.mitigation: Use short-lived tokens, revocation checks, audience binding, and continuous token introspection.

components.name: Agent Skills / MCP Registry
components.whatItIs: Reusable skills, MCP servers, manifests, and workflow packages that define what agents can do and how they do it.
components.whyItMatters: Agent Skills / MCP Registry helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.
whatCouldGoWrong: Malicious skill or MCP package installation

topRisks.name: Malicious skill or MCP package installation
topRisks.impact: A skill, plugin, or MCP server embeds harmful behavior that is trusted as reusable agent capability after installation.
topRisks.mitigation: Install only from verified publishers; scan behavior, scripts, manifests, and natural-language instructions before activation.

topRisks.name: Skill typosquatting / brand impersonation
topRisks.impact: A look-alike skill name or publisher tricks users or agents into installing an attacker-controlled package.
topRisks.mitigation: Verify publisher identity, package signing, reputation, namespace ownership, and exact dependency names.

topRisks.name: Unsigned or unpinned skill update
topRisks.impact: A previously safe skill silently changes behavior after an update, turning an approved capability into a supply-chain foothold.
topRisks.mitigation: Pin versions, require signed updates, diff manifests and instructions, and stage updates before production use.

components.name: Context Boundary & Provenance
components.whatItIs: Separates instructions from data and preserves evidence, source, and trust level as context moves across agents and tools.
components.whyItMatters: Context Boundary & Provenance helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Context boundary collapse
topRisks.impact: Untrusted data is treated as an instruction, policy, or trusted state, allowing an attacker to steer agent behavior indirectly.
topRisks.mitigation: Use explicit context labels and enforce instruction/data separation before model invocation and tool execution.

topRisks.name: Provenance loss across hops
topRisks.impact: As content moves through RAG, memory, tools, and agents, the system loses where it came from and why it should be trusted.
topRisks.mitigation: Carry provenance metadata with every context fragment and block trust elevation without verification.

topRisks.name: Evidence laundering through summaries
topRisks.impact: A false or malicious claim becomes credible after being summarized, cached, or cited by another agent.
topRisks.mitigation: Link summaries back to original evidence, distinguish claims from verified facts, and require source-level validation.

components.name: Model / Inference Routing
components.whatItIs: Selects model, prompt template, policy tier, context window, and fallback behavior for agent reasoning.
components.whyItMatters: Model / Inference Routing helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Prompt template injection
topRisks.impact: A compromised template or runtime variable injects hidden instructions before the agent even sees the user task.
topRisks.mitigation: Treat prompt templates as code, protect them with change control, signing, review, and runtime integrity checks.

topRisks.name: Unsafe model fallback
topRisks.impact: A failed or overloaded primary model falls back to a weaker model or policy tier without preserving safety constraints.
topRisks.mitigation: Define approved fallback tiers and require policy equivalence checks before automatic failover.

topRisks.name: Unbounded reasoning / denial of wallet
topRisks.impact: A task triggers excessive token use, repeated retries, or extended reasoning loops that consume cost and capacity.
topRisks.mitigation: Set token, cost, retry, and reasoning-duration budgets per task and per tenant.

components.name: Output & Egress Channels
components.whatItIs: Represents every route through which the agent sends content, files, actions, records, or instructions outward.
components.whyItMatters: Output & Egress Channels helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Covert exfiltration through normal output
topRisks.impact: Sensitive data is hidden inside an ordinary-looking summary, attachment, ticket, or generated file.
topRisks.mitigation: Inspect outbound content for sensitive data, abnormal destinations, and encoded or transformed payloads.

topRisks.name: Malicious generated artifact
topRisks.impact: The agent creates a file, script, link, or pull request that carries harmful behavior into another system.
topRisks.mitigation: Scan generated artifacts before release and require review for executable or automation-triggering outputs.

topRisks.name: Downstream automation abuse
topRisks.impact: A generated record or message triggers CI/CD, ticketing, workflow, or business automation in a way the user did not intend.
topRisks.mitigation: Apply policy gates at automation boundaries and require explicit approval for actions that can trigger downstream effects.

components.name: Agent Lifecycle & Governance
components.whatItIs: Tracks agent inventory, owners, versions, approvals, deployment state, rollback paths, and emergency disablement.
components.whyItMatters: Agent Lifecycle & Governance helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.
whatCouldGoWrong: Missing kill switch or rollback path

topRisks.name: Missing kill switch or rollback path
topRisks.impact: A compromised or misbehaving agent cannot be quickly stopped, isolated, or reverted during an incident.
topRisks.mitigation: Design emergency disablement, credential revocation, workflow pause, and configuration rollback into the runtime architecture.

topRisks.name: Shadow agents outside governance
topRisks.impact: Unapproved agents operate outside inventory, monitoring, risk review, and ownership controls.
topRisks.mitigation: Continuously discover agent workloads and require registration, owner assignment, and risk tiering before production use.

topRisks.name: Untracked agent version drift
topRisks.impact: Prompts, policies, tools, model versions, and skills drift across environments, making behavior hard to reproduce or secure.
topRisks.mitigation: Version prompts, tools, models, policies, and skills as release artifacts with promotion controls and change history.

components.name: Telemetry Integrity & Evidence
components.whatItIs: Captures tamper-resistant evidence of plans, prompts, retrieved context, tool calls, approvals, outputs, and policy decisions.
components.whyItMatters: Telemetry Integrity & Evidence helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Agent-generated telemetry tampering
topRisks.impact: A compromised agent alters logs, status reports, or records to hide what it actually did.
topRisks.mitigation: Write audit events to an append-only external store that agents cannot modify.

topRisks.name: Incomplete replayability
topRisks.impact: Investigators cannot reconstruct prompts, retrieved context, tool calls, approvals, or outputs after an incident.
topRisks.mitigation: Capture structured traces across planning, context retrieval, tool execution, approvals, and egress with sensitive-data controls.

topRisks.name: Non-repudiation failure
topRisks.impact: The organization cannot prove which agent, user, policy, or approval caused a high-impact action.
topRisks.mitigation: Bind actions to signed agent identity, user authority, policy decision, timestamp, and immutable evidence.

components.name: Guardrails & Monitoring
components.whatItIs: Policy enforcement, logging, and anomaly detection layered across the whole system.
components.whyItMatters: Guardrails & Monitoring helps the organization use agentic AI capabilities while preserving continuity, control, and accountability.

topRisks.name: Guardrail bypass via obfuscation
topRisks.impact: An attacker phrases a malicious instruction in a way that slips past pattern-based filters while still being understood by the model.
topRisks.mitigation: Layer semantic and behavioral detection on top of pattern matching, and test guardrails against adversarial phrasing.

topRisks.name: Blind spots / incomplete logging
topRisks.impact: Some agent actions or intermediate reasoning steps simply aren't logged, so an incident can't be fully reconstructed after the fact.
topRisks.mitigation: Log at every hop — planning, tool calls, and inter-agent messages — not just final outputs.

topRisks.name: Telemetry tampering / false audit trail
topRisks.impact: A compromised agent alters logs, status messages, or evidence records to hide what it did or mislead responders.
topRisks.mitigation: Write logs to append-only systems, preserve chain-of-custody, and verify agent reports against independent telemetry.

impacts.name: Operational Impact
impacts.description: The agent disrupts workflows, performs incorrect actions, or affects business continuity.

impacts.name: Financial Impact
impacts.description: The agent causes loss through fraud, unauthorized transactions, resource abuse, or service disruption.

impacts.name: Regulatory Impact
impacts.description: The agent mishandles data or actions in ways that create audit, privacy, safety, or compliance exposure.

impacts.name: Reputation Impact
impacts.description: The incident damages customer, partner, regulator, or employee trust.

impacts.name: Safety Impact
impacts.description: The agent influences physical-world, clinical, operational, or safety-sensitive decisions.
